headline: BOJ raises rate to 1.25%; BOJ governor: does not rule out consecutive or larger hikes | Sankei
summary: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate by 0.25 percentage point to 1.25%, the highest since 1995. Governor Kazuo Ueda said the bank will continue raising rates and does not rule out consecutive or larger hikes.
why: The Bank of Japan sets Japan's short-term interest rate, which influences the yen, Japanese government bond yields and global carry trades.
why_moved: The rate increase to the highest level since 1995, with the governor signalling further hikes are possible, shifts expectations for Japanese interest rates.
